now: authority weak; all-pass verified legal research is well under reliable; signature gated

extract.trigger: A contract file and one named clause type (for example indemnity or termination) are present. Quiet when no clause type is named, or when the ask is risk, compare, or edits.
extract.doneWhen: Each result row has a verbatim quote that is a substring of the source text and a section locator (section number, page, line). An empty result is valid: print "clause: none found in <sections searched>" and pass. One clause type per pass; a second type is a second pass.
extract.forbidden: Paraphrasing instead of quoting, or filling an empty result with a near clause. Write "none found" instead.

risk.trigger: A contract, one named party, and a written severity rule are present. The scoring party is the one the ask named, fixed for the whole pass (a second party is a second pass). Quiet when no party or no rule is given.
risk.doneWhen: Each score row carries the written rule it applied, a severity from that rule, and a verbatim quote that is a substring of the source with a section locator. A row without a quote is dropped and printed as "unscored: <text>". Zero scored rows is valid.
risk.forbidden: Scoring unquoted text, or scoring from both parties' views at once.
risk.gate: ABSENT sign (prepare the scored sheet and stop; a lawyer signs before anyone relies on it)

compare.trigger: A counterparty draft and a house paper are both present. Quiet when either is missing.
compare.doneWhen: The house paper clause list is the denominator. Each house clause yields exactly one row with status matched, changed, or missing; no row reads "fine" for silence. Output prints "rows: N; missing: M; changed: C; matched: K" with N equal to M+C+K and equal to the house clause count.
compare.forbidden: Treating a missing clause as fine, or dropping a row because the draft is silent.

draft.trigger: A flag naming one clause (flag id, section) and the original text are present. Quiet when no flag exists.
draft.doneWhen: The proposal is a tracked edit of the source. Reverting every tracked edit reproduces the source text byte for byte (original stays visible). Every edit hunk carries the flag id from the ask, and every changed line falls inside the flagged section's line range. A changed line outside the range, an untagged hunk, a hunk tagged with another flag id, or a revert that differs from the source fails. Zero edits is valid when the flag needs none.
draft.forbidden: Rewriting the deal: editing any clause the flag did not name.
draft.gate: ABSENT sign (prepare the flagged-clause edit and stop; a lawyer signs)

authority.trigger: A cite and the proposition it supports are present. Quiet when no cite or proposition is given.
authority.doneWhen: Each cite is resolved: it opens at a source, and the cite string (reporter cite, docket, or statute number) is a substring of the opened text, so the opened page is the cited authority. A quoted holding line with a page or paragraph locator must be a substring of that opened text. A candidate cite that does not open is dropped and printed "dropped: <cite>". Any cite kept or asserted in the output that did not open or resolve (invented), any quoted line not a substring of the opened text, or any pin locator that does not exist fails the card. Zero surviving cites is valid.
authority.forbidden: Keeping a cite that was not opened, or inventing a pin cite or holding quote.

diligence.trigger: A data room or document list and a stated scope are present. Quiet when scope is not stated.
diligence.doneWhen: Two lists print by document name, one per line: in-scope documents and not-read documents. A summary line "in scope: N; read: R; not read: U" prints with N equal to the number of in-scope names listed and equal to R plus U. A document with no read record is listed not-read, never implied-read. One sheet holds the issues: each row has a unique issue id and exactly one issue; every row's document name is in the read set (a not-read document has no row), and the printed row count equals the number of distinct issue ids.
diligence.forbidden: Implying a document was read because it sits in scope.
diligence.gate: ABSENT sign (prepare the coverage sheet and stop; a lawyer signs before anyone relies on it)
